name: Blotato
tagline: Turns one idea into platform-specific posts and videos, then publishes them to a dozen social accounts from one dashboard or API.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The AI half of Blotato is genuinely trivial: prompt a model to spin one source into an X thread, a LinkedIn post and a caption, then keep a queue in SQLite. The half that matters is publishing, and that half is not a coding problem, it is a platform approval problem. Posting to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook and LinkedIn on a schedule means registered apps, review submissions, business account requirements and tokens that rot on their own timetable. A large share of Blotato's actual customers are automation tinkerers who already built the drafting part themselves and pay purely for the posting endpoint. You can build a very pleasant personal version that publishes to Bluesky, Mastodon and Telegram and hands you clipboard text for everything else, which is a different product.
coreLoopDIY: Paste a source, have an LLM generate per-platform variants from editable prompt templates, queue them on a calendar, and auto-publish to the few platforms whose auth is a token rather than a review process.
requirements: Bluesky app password, Mastodon token, Telegram bot token, or a Discord webhook for the automatable targets
A machine or cheap VPS that stays awake for the scheduler
Willingness to paste manually into Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn
whatYouLose: Automated publishing to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Threads and Pinterest, which is the entire point
Someone else eating the breakage every time a platform changes its API or revokes a token
AI video generation with stock footage, captions and voiceover attached
A hosted API you can call from n8n or Make without running your own box
Media hosting and per-platform format handling: aspect ratios, durations, size caps
moatNotes: The barrier is not code, it is being an approved publishing app on platforms that gatekeep write access and change the rules quarterly.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the thing they need is write access to closed platforms, and you cannot self-host that. Getting Instagram Graph API or TikTok content posting approved for a one-person setup ranges from tedious to flatly not worth it, and once approved you inherit the maintenance: token refreshes, deprecated endpoints, silent rate limits, format rules that differ per surface. Blotato sells a single endpoint that absorbs all of it, which is why it shows up as a node in other people's automations rather than as the whole workflow. If your posting surface is Bluesky, Mastodon and a newsletter, none of that applies and you should build it.
notes: Drafting the posts is the easy half, and an agent will nail it in an afternoon. The moat is approved write access across a dozen walled platforms plus the unglamorous work of keeping it alive when each one breaks.
prompt:
Build a local-first social content repurposer and publishing queue called "postpile".

Stack: TypeScript, Node 20, SQLite via better-sqlite3, one small Express server with server-rendered HTML plus htmx. No React, no bundler, no build step beyond tsc. Start with `npm run dev`, database at ./data/postpile.db.

In scope:
1. Add a source: pasted text, a URL that gets fetched and stripped to readable text, or a local transcript file.
2. Generate variants by calling an OpenAI-compatible API, base URL and key from .env. Targets: X thread, LinkedIn post, Instagram caption with hashtags, short-form video hook script, newsletter blurb.
3. Keep one prompt template per target as editable markdown in ./prompts so voice can be tuned without touching code.
4. Queue table with columns: source_id, platform, body, media_paths, scheduled_at, status, attempts.
5. Editor view per queued item with a live character counter and a hard per-platform cap.
6. Real publish adapters for the platforms with token auth only: Bluesky via AT Protocol app password, Mastodon via access token, Telegram channel via bot token, Discord via webhook. One adapter interface, each adapter pure and unit tested against a fake HTTP client.
7. For X, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube do not pretend. Implement a "manual handoff" adapter that renders copy-ready text, lists media files to download, and marks the item posted only when I confirm.
8. A node-cron worker in the same process that publishes due items, retries three times with exponential backoff, and writes every attempt to a runs table.
9. Calendar view for the next 30 days, plus a dead-letter list.

Out of scope: user accounts, multi-tenancy, OAuth flows, analytics scraping, AI video generation, hosted media, mobile app, telemetry of any kind.

Rules: every secret in .env with a committed .env.example, no network calls at import time, a seed script with three fake sources, and a README that states plainly which platforms this can automate and which it cannot, with the reason being platform approval rather than missing code.
